e-7408.knowledge_point: Solving a Logistic Growth Initial Value Problem
e-7408.problem:
The rate of growth of the panda population $P(t)$ in a particular forest follows the logistic growth model is

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = 0.001\,25 P(800-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the beginning of the observations. Find an expression for the panda population after $t$ years, given that there were $400$ pandas initially.
e-7408.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = kP(a-P),
$$

where $k > 0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a > P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t) = \dfrac{a}{1+Ce^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.001\,25,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=800.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t) 
= \dfrac{800}{1+Ce^{-(800\cdot 0.001\,25)t}}= \dfrac{800}{1+Ce^{-t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=400$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{800}{1+C{e}^{-0}} & =400 \\ \frac{800}{1+C} & =400 \\ \frac{1+C}{800} & =\frac{1}{400} \\ 1+C & =\frac{800}{400} \\ C & =2-1 \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the panda population is given by

$$
P(t)= \dfrac{800}{1+e^{-t}} .
$$

e-7407.knowledge_point: Using the Particular Solution of a Logistic Growth Initial Value Problem to Make Predictions
e-7407.problem: The growth rate of the hare population $P(t)$ in a particular forest is jointly proportional to the hare population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the forest's carrying capacity and the hare population. The constant of proportionality is $0.000\,01$ and the carrying capacity is $10\,000.$ How many hares will there be in the forest after $7$ years given that there were $2\,500$ hares initially? Round your answer to the nearest integer.
e-7407.worked_solution:
Since the hare population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the hare population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the hare population, the hare population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = kP(a-P),
$$

where $k > 0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a > P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t) = \dfrac{a}{1+Ce^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality $k=0.000\,01,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=10\,000.$ Therefore, the hare population is given by the equation

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t} = 0.000\,01 P(10\,000-P) .
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t) 
= \dfrac{10\,000}{1+Ce^{-(10\,000\cdot 0.000\,01)t}}= \dfrac{10\,000}{1+Ce^{-0.1t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=2\,500$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =2\,500 \\ \frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.1(0)}} & =2\,500 \\ \frac{10\,000}{1+C} & =2\,500 \\ \frac{1+C}{10\,000} & =\frac{1}{2\,500} \\ 1+C & =\frac{10\,000}{2\,500} \\ 1+C & =4 \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t) = \frac{10\,000}{1+3 e^{-0.1 t}}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of hares in the forest after $7$ years, we substitute $t=7$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(7) & =\frac{10\,000}{1+3{e}^{-0.1\cdot 7}} \\  & ≈4\,016.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The rate of growth of the bear population $P(t)$ in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.2P(4\,500-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after $t$ years, given that there were $150$ bears initially.
after.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.2,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=4\,500.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-(4\,500\cdot 0.2)t}}=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=150$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900\cdot 0}} & =150 \\ 1+C & =\frac{4\,500}{150} \\ C & =30-1 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+29{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

Question 1
?

The rate of growth of the bear population P(t) in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

dPdt=0.2P(4500−P),

where t is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after t years, given that there were 150 bears initially.

a
P(t)=45001−29e−900t
b
P(t)=45001+29e−900t
c
P(t)=45001+29e−90t
d
P(t)=45001+150e−900t
e
P(t)=30001−29e−900t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A logistic growth equation has the form

dPdt=kP(a−P),

where k>0 is a constant of proportionality, and a>P is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt.

In this case, the constant of proportionality is k=0.2, and the carrying capacity is a=4500.

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

P(t)=45001+Ce−(4500⋅0.2)t=45001+Ce−900t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=150 and solve for C. We get

45001+Ce−900⋅0=1501+C=4500150C=30−1=29.

So, we have

P(t)=45001+29e−900t.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b. The logistic solution has exponent -akt=-900t, and P(0)=150 gives C=4500/150-1=29. Therefore P(t)=4500/(1+29e^{-900t}), which satisfies both the differential equation and initial condition.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Logistic Growth Initial Value Problem
content.problem:
The rate of growth of the bear population $P(t)$ in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.2P(4\,500-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after $t$ years, given that there were $150$ bears initially.
content.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.2,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=4\,500.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-(4\,500\cdot 0.2)t}}=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=150$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900\cdot 0}} & =150 \\ 1+C & =\frac{4\,500}{150} \\ C & =30-1 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+29{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

The rate of growth in the number of fishes P(t) with a fungal infection in a certain pond is jointly proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time t and the number that have not been infected. If the constant of proportionality is 0.009 and the carrying capacity is 130, then find an expression for the number of fishes with fungal infection, given that there were 5 fishes infected initially.

a
P(t)=1301+25e−0.009t
b
P(t)=1301+25e−1.17t
c
P(t)=251+e−t
d
P(t)=251+e−0.009t
e
P(t)=51+25e−1.17t
Submit

decision.explanation: Joint proportionality gives dP/dt=0.009P(130-P). Its logistic solution is P(t)=130/(1+Ce^{-1.17t}), since 130(0.009)=1.17. Using P(0)=5 gives C=130/5-1=25, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The rate of growth in the number of fishes $P(t)$ with a fungal infection in a certain pond is jointly proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time $t$ and the number that have not been infected. If the constant of proportionality is $0.009$ and the carrying capacity is $130,$ then find an expression for the number of fishes with fungal infection, given that there were $5$ fishes infected initially.
after.worked_solution:
Since the growth rate of infected fishes is *jointly* proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time $t,$ and the number that have not, the number of infected fishes follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.009,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=130.$ Therefore, the growth of the number of fishes with fungal infection is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.009P(130-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-(130\cdot 0.009)t}}=\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-1.17t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=5$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-1.17\cdot 0}} & =5 \\ 1+C & =\frac{130}{5} \\ C & =26-1 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{130}{1+25{e}^{-1.17t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The rate of growth in the number of fishes P(t) with a fungal infection in a certain pond is jointly proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time t and the number that have not been infected. If the constant of proportionality is 0.009 and the carrying capacity is 130, then find an expression for the number of fishes with fungal infection, given that there were 5 fishes infected initially.

a
P(t)=1301+25e−0.009t
b
P(t)=1301+25e−1.17t
c
P(t)=251+e−t
d
P(t)=251+e−0.009t
e
P(t)=51+25e−1.17t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the growth rate of infected fishes is jointly proportional to the number of fishes that have been infected at time t, and the number that have not, the number of infected fishes follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

dPdt=kP(a−P),

where k>0 is a constant of proportionality, and a>P is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt.

In this case, the constant of proportionality is k=0.009, and the carrying capacity is a=130. Therefore, the growth of the number of fishes with fungal infection is given by the equation

dPdt=0.009P(130−P).

The general solution to this equation is

P(t)=1301+Ce−(130⋅0.009)t=1301+Ce−1.17t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=5 and solve for C. We get

1301+Ce−1.17⋅0=51+C=1305C=26−1=25.

So, we have

P(t)=1301+25e−1.17t.

$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{130}{1+C{e}^{-1.17\cdot 0}} & =5 \\ 1+C & =\frac{130}{5} \\ C & =26-1 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{130}{1+25{e}^{-1.17t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The growth rate of the mouse population P(t) in a certain field is jointly proportional to the mouse population at time t, measured in years, and the difference between the field's carrying capacity and the mouse population. If the constant of proportionality is 0.0000625 and the carrying capacity is 8000, then find an expression for the mouse population after t years, given that there were 1000 mice in the field initially.

a
P(t)=80001+5e−0.5t
b
P(t)=80001+5e−0.2t
c
P(t)=80001+4e−2t
d
P(t)=80001+7e−0.5t
e
P(t)=80001+4e−0.1t
Submit

decision.explanation: The logistic solution is P(t)=8000/(1+Ce^{-akt}), where ak=8000(0.0000625)=0.5. The initial condition gives C=8000/1000-1=7. Therefore option d satisfies the model and initial population.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The growth rate of the mouse population $P(t)$ in a certain field is jointly proportional to the mouse population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the field's carrying capacity and the mouse population. If the constant of proportionality is $0.000\,062\,5$ and the carrying capacity is $8\,000,$ then find an expression for the mouse population after $t$ years, given that there were $1\,000$ mice in the field initially.
after.worked_solution:
Since the mouse population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the mouse population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the mouse population, the mouse population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,062\,5,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=8\,000.$ Therefore, the mouse population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.000\,062\,5P(8\,000-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(8\,000\cdot 0.000\,062\,5)t}}=\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.5t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=1\,000$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.5\cdot 0}} & =1\,000 \\ 1+C & =\frac{8\,000}{1\,000} \\ C & =8-1 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{8\,000}{1+7{e}^{-0.5t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

The growth rate of the mouse population P(t) in a certain field is jointly proportional to the mouse population at time t, measured in years, and the difference between the field's carrying capacity and the mouse population. If the constant of proportionality is 0.0000625 and the carrying capacity is 8000, then find an expression for the mouse population after t years, given that there were 1000 mice in the field initially.

a
P(t)=80001+5e−0.5t
b
P(t)=80001+5e−0.2t
c
P(t)=80001+4e−2t
d
P(t)=80001+7e−0.5t
e
P(t)=80001+4e−0.1t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the mouse population's growth rate is jointly proportional to the mouse population at time t and the difference between the carrying capacity and the mouse population, the mouse population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

dPdt=kP(a−P),

where k>0 is a constant of proportionality, and a>P is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt.

In this case, the constant of proportionality is k=0.0000625, and the carrying capacity is a=8000. Therefore, the mouse population growth is given by the equation

dPdt=0.0000625P(8000−P).

The general solution to this equation is

P(t)=80001+Ce−(8000⋅0.0000625)t=80001+Ce−0.5t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=1000 and solve for C. We get

80001+Ce−0.5⋅0=10001+C=80001000C=8−1=7.

So, we have

P(t)=80001+7e−0.5t.

content.problem: The growth rate of the mouse population $P(t)$ in a certain field is jointly proportional to the mouse population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the field's carrying capacity and the mouse population. If the constant of proportionality is $0.000\,062\,5$ and the carrying capacity is $8\,000,$ then find an expression for the mouse population after $t$ years, given that there were $1\,000$ mice in the field initially.
content.worked_solution:
Since the mouse population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the mouse population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the mouse population, the mouse population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,062\,5,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=8\,000.$ Therefore, the mouse population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.000\,062\,5P(8\,000-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(8\,000\cdot 0.000\,062\,5)t}}=\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.5t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=1\,000$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.5\cdot 0}} & =1\,000 \\ 1+C & =\frac{8\,000}{1\,000} \\ C & =8-1 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{8\,000}{1+7{e}^{-0.5t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The growth rate of the crab population P(t) in a certain river is jointly proportional to the crab population at time t, measured in years, and the difference between the river's carrying capacity and the crab population. If the constant of proportionality is 0.00002 and the carrying capacity is 10000, then find an expression for the crab population after t years, given that there were 1000 crab in the river initially.

a
P(t)=100001+4e−2t
b
P(t)=100001+5e−0.2t
c
P(t)=100001+4e−0.1t
d
P(t)=100001+9e−0.2t
e
P(t)=100001+5e−2t
Submit

decision.explanation: The logistic solution is P(t)=a/(1+Ce^{-akt}). Here ak=10000(0.00002)=0.2, and P(0)=1000 gives C=10000/1000-1=9. Thus option d satisfies the model and initial condition.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The growth rate of the crab population $P(t)$ in a certain river is jointly proportional to the crab population at time $t,$ measured in years, and the difference between the river's carrying capacity and the crab population. If the constant of proportionality is $0.000\,02$ and the carrying capacity is $10\,000,$ then find an expression for the crab population after $t$ years, given that there were $1\,000$ crab in the river initially.
after.worked_solution:
Since the crab population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the crab population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the crab population, the crab population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,02,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=10\,000.$ Therefore, the crab population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.000\,02P(10\,000-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(10\,000\cdot 0.000\,02t)}}=\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=1\,000$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2\cdot 0}} & =1\,000 \\ 1+C & =\frac{10\,000}{1\,000} \\ C & =10-1 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{10\,000}{1+9{e}^{-0.2t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

The growth rate of the crab population P(t) in a certain river is jointly proportional to the crab population at time t, measured in years, and the difference between the river's carrying capacity and the crab population. If the constant of proportionality is 0.00002 and the carrying capacity is 10000, then find an expression for the crab population after t years, given that there were 1000 crab in the river initially.

a
P(t)=100001+4e−2t
b
P(t)=100001+5e−0.2t
c
P(t)=100001+4e−0.1t
d
P(t)=100001+9e−0.2t
e
P(t)=100001+5e−2t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the crab population's growth rate is jointly proportional to the crab population at time t and the difference between the carrying capacity and the crab population, the crab population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

dPdt=kP(a−P),

where k>0 is a constant of proportionality, and a>P is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt.

In this case, the constant of proportionality is k=0.00002, and the carrying capacity is a=10000. Therefore, the crab population growth is given by the equation

dPdt=0.00002P(10000−P).

The general solution to this equation is

P(t)=100001+Ce−(10000⋅0.00002t)=100001+Ce−0.2t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=1000 and solve for C. We get

100001+Ce−0.2⋅0=10001+C=100001000C=10−1=9.

So, we have

P(t)=100001+9e−0.2t.

content.worked_solution:
Since the crab population's growth rate is *jointly* proportional to the crab population at time $t$ and the difference between the carrying capacity and the crab population, the crab population follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,02,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=10\,000.$ Therefore, the crab population growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.000\,02P(10\,000-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(10\,000\cdot 0.000\,02t)}}=\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=1\,000$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10\,000}{1+C{e}^{-0.2\cdot 0}} & =1\,000 \\ 1+C & =\frac{10\,000}{1\,000} \\ C & =10-1 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t)=\frac{10\,000}{1+9{e}^{-0.2t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.05P-0.000\,5{P}^{2} \\  & =0.000\,5P(100-P)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,5,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=100.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-(100\cdot 0.000\,5)t}}=\frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-0.05t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=5$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =5 \\ \frac{100}{1+C{e}^{-0.05(0)}} & =5 \\ 1+C & =20 \\ C & =19\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{100}{1+19{e}^{-0.05t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=11$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(11) & =\frac{100}{1+19{e}^{-0.05(11)}} \\  & ≈8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $11$ years, approximately $8$ turtles inhabited the island.
